name: Qoves analysis

lead: Qoves analysis refers to the facial assessment offered by Qoves, an online aesthetics service. Users upload photos and receive measurements of facial features, scores and a plan of suggested non-surgical changes such as skincare, grooming and habits.
The idea is to turn a face into a list of specific, trackable things to improve. The company describes its method as drawing on hundreds of methods; no independent trial of its results is published.

paras: The company says users upload six photos of the face and head and receive results within about 28 days, delivered through a dashboard with messaging to a care team, visual previews and an annual re-analysis, sold as a yearly membership.
The service says it is not a clinical or medical service and that results vary. Scores are the company's own metrics, and generated previews may not match real outcomes.

chain: Photos are measured against facial markers
Weaknesses are listed with a non-surgical plan
angle.text: The service converts photos into specific measurements and a plan of skincare, grooming and habit changes, with previews of intended outcomes. Gains come from the changes a user then makes.

lead: Qoves analysis is the facial assessment sold by Qoves, an online service that describes itself as offering a personalized facial analysis and a non-surgical "glow-up" plan delivered remotely.[1]

According to the company, users submit six photos; it says it measures over 160 facial markers including symmetry, proportions, skin quality and brow density, then returns biometric scores, a protocol of skincare, grooming and habit changes with suggested costs and timelines, visualizations of possible changes and yearly updates.[1]

The company's claims about helping attractiveness and its use of 450+ evidence-based methods are its own marketing; it states it is not a licensed medical service.[1] In looksmaxxing circles, "Qoves" is also used as shorthand for this style of measurement-based facial analysis.

paras: The service is offered through the company's website and described as remote: photo upload, a dashboard with biometric scores that can be tracked over time, and messaging with a care team.[1]
Scores listed by the company include facial femininity, symmetry and proportionality.[1]

Qoves states it is not a licensed clinical or medical service, that any medical treatment should be discussed with a licensed provider, and that some images are digitally generated and results vary.[1]
